Hi Althoufx,

My first trade (short) was a success, although I closed it way too soon. After closing the trade I re-labeled the chart (based on a mistake in reading an engulf when there wasn't one) and so my long trade was stopped out. Prior to making this mistake, here is what I saw on my chart that prompted me to go short at that level:

PA formed two bearish engulfs, and price formed a DM in lose proximity to the MPL. I didn't know for sure that price wouldn't keep moving up, but my stop loss was tiny so I took it. In hindsight, I wish I would have kept the trade running. There was no reason to close it...especially since EG # 1 opened a nice downside target (to at least around 117.714-ish.

This target was also engulfed, so if I was watching the trade and actively managing it, I would have stayed in it.

One of my biggest weaknesses is second guessing my analysis midway through a trade. This problem worsens when I watch too many charts at one time.

So.. I was wrong about UJ.

Here is how I managed the trade to avoid loss: I am finding that knowledge of ORFL's and TD/TS is helpful in knowing when to bail from a bad trade. Often times we get a nice RT after an engulf/FO of an important level which gives us a chance to bail without a loss.

In this case, my entry was executed when I wasn't watching the screen. When I saw price engulfed the scale ORFL up and TD on reaction (past the QM level that is neon green) I knew price was likely to drop further and got out for a small profit.

Price dropped through the zone and I am now flat. I will look at this and try to find out what happened. It may be that Jurij was right and price wants to drop a bit lower to the edge of the zone that is more clear on the Daily chart he posted yesterday. I have to take a closer look at this.

posts.t:
This is something I have been focusing on lately:

Simply looking for a DM to occur at TS/TD.

Make sure the HH of the QM touches the SR of the TS zone and bounces away nicely. The DM is the deeper RT (close to or exactly at the MPL). Tight stop loss and decent R:R.

This is what I did for the UJ scalp I posted above.

I am still in the process of refining this strategy, but I like TS and TD because they have the MPL. The MPL gives us an exact entry with almost no stop loss. If wrong, it is a minimal loss. If correct, the trade has great RR.

When adding the LTF PA in to choose ones with a DM formation increases the odds for a bounce.

Next step: check scales to see where price is coming from to filter out trades that get taken in the wrong direction to the higher TF targets.

All combined, this could be a very profitable strategy that can be consistently applied to the charts.

افزودن PA تایم‌فریم پایین برای انتخاب مواردی که DM در آن‌ها شکل می‌گیرد، احتمال برگشت را بیشتر می‌کند.

Addition to my drawing on post # 1538 above:

Scale is important, and critical to knowing which break of SD or TS is an engulf. The trick occurs in the form of a DM in the TS zone @ the MPL. Why? Because price is coming from an unreached target for sellers we know to look for sells only..and we expect price to trick/FO and the extreme end of the PAZ to trick retailers to buying at the worst place possible so the IT's can sell in to all the buy orders.

They want liquidity and they want to be the only ones short. to do this they have to shake out all of the riffraff

I will remember to revisit this soon, when I become more comfortable labeling the origins and TD/TS.

...correlations i know they are results of algorithms, that specially refer to the "values" of the moves. They have no meaning in RTM.

i was thinking to EURUSD that should move (....actually it does it, in real time too...) in a way opposite to UJ and UC, specially when these ones move in synchronism. Simply moves higher or lower. Nothing about values........EU won't move in the same direction of USDCHF/USDJPY, specially in mid-high TF... it's enough to take a look of a chart by EU compared with same TF charts by USDCHF/USDJPY and to see how significant this comparison can be. For example when EU charts does not have a clear, "screaming" bearish/bullish evolution, i would watch UCH/UJ too, looking for further signal more clear/evident (if any), to be taken in the opposite direction.

کاش پاسخم برای موضوع همبستگی‌ها (فکر می‌کنم سؤال تو همین را می‌پرسد) بهتر بود. دربارهٔ EUR-USD و USD-JPY و USD-CHF در زمینهٔ همبستگی‌ها چیزی نمی‌دانم. همیشه متوجه شده‌ام:

EUR-USD و USD-CHF تمایل دارند همبستگی منفی داشته باشند.

USD-CHF و USD-JPY تمایل دارند همبستگی مثبت داشته باشند.

من آدمِ درستی نیستم که دربارهٔ اعمال این به تحلیل RTM بپرسم

فکر می‌کنم ایدهٔ خوبی است که این را وارد کنم و اگر پیشرفته‌تر بودم، قطعاً از همبستگی برای فیلتر کردن معاملاتم استفاده می‌کردم. الان با زحمت می‌توانم یک نمودار را تحلیل کنم و برای افزودن همبستگی‌ها باید آن‌ها را مقایسه کنم تا خطاهای ممکن در تحلیلم را فیلتر کنم.

یادم می‌ماند که به‌زودی به این برگردم، وقتی برچسب‌گذاری مبدأها و TD/TS برایم راحت‌تر شد.

… دربارهٔ همبستگی‌ها، می‌دانم که نتیجهٔ الگوریتم‌ها هستند و مخصوصاً به «مقادیر» حرکت‌ها مربوط‌اند. در RTM معنایی ندارند.

در مورد EURUSD فکر می‌کردم که باید به شیوه‌ای برعکس UJ و UC حرکت کند (… در واقع همین‌طور هم می‌کند، در زمان واقعی هم… ) مخصوصاً وقتی این دو هماهنگ حرکت می‌کنند. فقط بالاتر یا پایین‌تر حرکت می‌کند. چیزی دربارهٔ مقادیر نیست… EU در جهت USDCHF/USDJPY حرکت نمی‌کند، مخصوصاً در تایم‌فریم میانی-بالا… کافی است به یک چارت EU نگاه کنی و آن را با چارت‌های همان تایم‌فریم برای USDCHF/USDJPY مقایسه کنی تا ببینی این مقایسه چقدر می‌تواند معنادار باشد. برای مثال وقتی چارت‌های EU تحول نزولی/صعودی واضح و «فریادزننده» ندارد، من هم UCH/UJ را تماشا می‌کنم، به دنبال سیگنال بعدی واضح‌تر/بیرون‌زده‌تر (اگر هست) برای گرفتن در جهت مخالف.
